open_points.subject: A17 configuration item names
open_points.text:
The items are exactly these: the store's
   location; the backup location and the backup key (A18); the owner
   credential; one service token for each service of A09 — PresuPro, Client
   Portal, Cabinet, Cabinet Kernel (R0-20, R0-23) — or, for an owner-only
   start, none of the four
open_points.question: What is the exact, case-sensitive environment-variable name for each listed item, and are any aliases accepted?
options: Declare one fixed environment-variable name for every item and accept no aliases.
Derive names mechanically from the prose item names.
Accept multiple aliases for an item.
open_points.default_guess: Declare one uppercase `REGISTRY_` name per item, accept only exact matches, and treat every other name as an ignored extra.

witness.initial: The store, backup directory, and all required secrets are valid, but no exact environment-variable mapping has been declared.
events: The owner supplies the store location as `REGISTRY_STORE_PATH`.
Registry starts and reads its configuration.
outcomes: An implementation that chose `REGISTRY_STORE_PATH` accepts the item and continues.
An implementation that chose `REGISTRY_STORE_LOCATION` reports the store location missing and stops.

open_points.subject: A17 misspelt service-token variable
open_points.text:
a variable whose name names none of them —
   one beginning with `REGISTRY_` included — is neither read nor checked and
   does not stop the start (owner, 2026-11-11: only the one module that reads
   the environment sees it, and it reads the items it declares; a misspelt
   name still stops the start, as the item it was meant to set is then
   missing)
open_points.question: If the owner supplies only a misspelt service-token variable, so that none of the four declared service-token items is present, does Registry start owner-only under the all-four-or-none rule, or stop because a misspelt name must stop the start?
options: Ignore the misspelt variable and start owner-only because none of the four declared tokens is present.
Stop and name the intended service token as missing.
Limit the claim that a misspelling stops startup to mandatory non-token items and to partial recognized token sets.
open_points.default_guess: Ignore the unknown variable and start owner-only, then narrow the misspelling statement to cases where the declared-item checks actually require the missing item.

witness.initial: Every mandatory non-service item is valid, and none of the four canonical service-token variables is present.
events: The owner intends to configure PresuPro but supplies a misspelling of PresuPro's token variable.
Registry performs the service-token all-four-or-none check.
outcomes: The unknown-variable and all-four-or-none rules yield a valid owner-only start.
The statement that a misspelt name still stops startup yields a failed start naming the PresuPro token as missing.

open_points.subject: A17 configuration access
open_points.text:
The configuration is a set of environment variables whose names begin
   with `REGISTRY_`, set as R0-23 says. Registry reads exactly the items
   below and no other variable
open_points.rule: Таблица выше — исчерпывающий список путей значения, и у каждого из них своя форма: перечисление называется адресом, константа поставщика — `the imported X constant`, настройка — полем объекта настроек.
open_points.question: The passage must name these environment-dependent launch settings as fields of the settings object supplied through the configuration module, rather than leave generated Registry code to read raw environment variables directly.
